post.caption: Graff's blue diamond once lacked a name. The Wittelsbach Blue diamond once sat on Bavaria's royal crown and weighed about 35 carats. In 1958, it stood unnamed at the Brussels World's Fair. Heirs of the dealer who owned it wanted it recut, but the jeweler they asked, Joseph Komkommer, recognized it and refused. In 2008, Laurence Graff bought it at Christie's in London and had it recut, and it lost about 4.5 carats. GIA regraded it as Internally Flawless. Today it is called the Wittelsbach Graff and weighs 31.06 carats.
